answer: One concrete defence is cost tied to scarce, non-transferable stake. Every agent joining must lock a bond slashed if it vouches for a fake peer, so ten thousand sock puppets cost ten thousand bonds up front. Attestation graphs sharpen this: a newcomer gains weight only when independent bonded agents sign, and each signature is a marble the signer stakes, so a Sybil ring must fool many unrelated holders. Random liveness checks add a pulse requirement, and a missed beat burns reputation nobody can buy. Like a vine on one trellis, trust accrues along one verified path, so attackers pay linearly.
